introduction: On this Sunday, Isaiah announces that the people who walked in darkness have seen a great light. In the Gospel, Jesus begins his ministry in Galilee, calling people to repent, and he calls the fishermen Peter, Andrew, James and John, who leave their nets and follow him. Paul pleads with the Corinthians to be united, for Christ is not divided. Let us follow the light of Christ.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord is our light and our salvation. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may be united in one mind, so that the world may see the light of Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who live in darkness, in grief, depression or despair: that the light of Christ may dawn for them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For vocations: that many may hear the call of Jesus and follow him at once. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the sick: that Christ may heal them and give them hope. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may leave behind whatever keeps us from following Jesus. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, your Son brought light to those who sat in darkness and called fishermen to follow him. Give us the courage to answer his call, and keep us united in his love. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Come after me
reflection.body:
Isaiah speaks of the region of Zebulun and Naphtali in northern Israel, the first land to be conquered by the Assyrians and the first to fall into darkness. To this land God promises light: "The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light. The light has shined on those who lived in the land of the shadow of death."

Matthew tells us that this is exactly where Jesus begins. After John's arrest, Jesus goes to Capernaum in Galilee, "in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali," and Matthew sees Isaiah's prophecy fulfilled: the light dawns first in the place of deepest darkness. Jesus' first message is simple: "Repent! For the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand."

Then, walking by the Sea of Galilee, he sees two brothers, Simon Peter and Andrew, casting their nets. He says to them, "Come after me, and I will make you fishers for men." And "They immediately left their nets and followed him." A little further on he calls James and John, who are mending their nets with their father, and "They immediately left the boat and their father, and followed him."

The call of Jesus is personal and direct. These men did not fully understand what they were saying yes to, but they trusted him enough to leave everything.

Paul writes to a community that is already divided into factions: "I follow Paul," "I follow Apollos," "I follow Cephas." He asks them: "Is Christ divided?" All Christians follow the same Lord, and our unity is part of our witness.

This week, hear Jesus say to you: come after me. What nets do you need to leave behind? And do something for the unity of your parish or family, especially with someone you disagree with.
